Implemented. The crate was a 41-line stub; it now loads anchors from the platform store with a portable backend plus two per-OS ones.

Design is portable-first per the user's steer ('not nailed to an OS, but linux will probably be the primary target'). The default reader handles PEM bundles and cert directories -- not a Linux feature, but how trust is exposed on Linux, Android, the BSDs, illumos, every container image, and macOS with Homebrew/Nix. No FFI, so it compiles and is tested everywhere. Keychain and CryptoAPI layer on top as per-target deps.

Resolved a contradiction in the process: this stub declared Linux out of scope ('a PEM file at a well-known path, consumers read it directly') while PKIX-77k9.2 lists Linux as priority #1. The stub's premise is wrong -- it is eight paths across Debian/RHEL/SUSE/Alpine/FreeBSD/illumos/Android plus SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR. The epic was right.

Two decisions carry the value. Environment variables beat anything on disk and a broken one errors rather than falling back, because a caller who set SSL_CERT_FILE made a decision. And loading is lenient with a report: from_pem is all-or-nothing, so one odd certificate in a distro's 122 would yield zero anchors instead of 121 -- LoadReport::skipped keeps that visible rather than silent, which is what makes this worth more than a from_pem_file call.

Also answered PKIX-tit4.5 for this crate: IoFailure::from_io is already public, so IoFailure is re-exported rather than duplicated.

ONE CRATE, NOT ONE PER OS -- asked and decided. Cargo's target-specific dependencies already mean a Linux build never compiles or audits security-framework, so the usual reason to split does not apply; splitting would instead push a cfg cascade onto every consumer, which is the boilerplate this crate exists to delete. Matches rustls-native-certs and the existing pkix-aia-http / pkix-net-guard pattern in this workspace. pkix-truststore-pkcs11 stays separate because it is a different trust model (slots, tokens, PINs), not a different OS.

9 tests, aimed at degradation rather than the happy path, plus agreement with the strict loader on this host's real 122-cert store. Added to the typos gate. 2339 workspace tests green; fmt, clippy, rustdoc and the --depth 2 powerset clean.

UNVERIFIED, stated in the crate docs and both module headers: the macOS/iOS and Windows backends have never been compiled. They parse (rustc on each file reports only unresolved imports) and every call was written against signatures read from security-framework 3.7.0 and schannel 0.1.30 rather than recalled, but no Apple or Windows toolchain was available. The Windows one also knowingly does not subtract the DISALLOWED store. Follow-up work is to finish them on a machine that can build them. Commit 739cabb4.
